questions.text: किसी विलेय के 2.0 मोलल जलीय विलयन में उसका मोल-अंश होता है:
questions.text_english: The mole fraction of a solute in 2.0 molal aqueous solution is:
questions.solution: A 2.0 molal solution means 2.0 moles of solute dissolved in 1000 g (55.5 moles) of water. Mole fraction of solute = 2.0 / (2.0 + 55.5) = 2.0 / 57.5 = 0.0347. Options A and B are far too large for a dilute solution, and option D is too small. Therefore, the correct answer is (C) 0.0347.

questions.text: प्लैटिनम इलेक्ट्रोडों के साथ NaCl के अति तनुजलीय विलयन का विद्युत-अपघटन करने पर:
questions.text_english: On electrolysis of very dilute aqueous solution of NaCl using platinum electrodes:

options.A: ऐनोड पर H2 गैस उत्सर्जित होती है।
options.B: कैथोड पर Na उत्पादित होता है।
options.C: ऐनोड पर O2 गैस उत्सर्जित होती है।
options.D: कैथोड पर H2 गैस उत्सर्जित होती है।

options_english.A: H2 gas is evolved at anode.
options_english.C: O2 gas is evolved at anode.
options_english.D: H2 gas is evolved at cathode.

questions.solution: In very dilute aqueous NaCl, water molecules are present in large excess. At the cathode, H+ ions (from water) are preferentially discharged over Na+ ions because Na+ has a much higher reduction potential, producing H2 gas. At the anode, in very dilute solution, OH- ions (from water) are oxidised in preference to Cl- ions, producing O2. However, the question asks what happens at cathode specifically — H2 is evolved at cathode. Option (D) is correct. Option A is wrong (H2 is not at anode), option B is wrong (Na is not deposited from aqueous solution), option C is partially true for dilute solution anode but D correctly identifies cathode behaviour.
questions.solution_hindi: अति तनु जलीय NaCl में, कैथोड पर H+ आयन (जल से) अपचयित होकर H2 गैस देते हैं, क्योंकि Na+ का अपचयन जलीय माध्यम में संभव नहीं। अतः सही उत्तर (D) है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित यौगिकों में से कौन-सा जलीय NaOH के साथ नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रियाओं के प्रति सर्वाधिक अभिक्रियाशील है?
questions.text_english: Which of the following compounds is most reactive towards nucleophilic substitution reaction with aqueous NaOH?
questions.solution: Nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) is facilitated by electron-withdrawing groups on the benzene ring. In option (D), 2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene has two strong electron-withdrawing nitro groups at ortho and para positions relative to the Cl, which greatly stabilise the Meisenheimer complex intermediate, making it highly reactive towards SNAr. Options B and C have electron-donating groups (methyl and methoxy) which deactivate the ring. Option A (benzyl chloride) undergoes SN1/SN2 at the aliphatic carbon, not aromatic SNAr. Hence (D) is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: नाभिकरागी ऐरोमैटिक प्रतिस्थापन इलेक्ट्रॉन-अपसारी समूहों द्वारा सुगम होता है। (D) में दो नाइट्रो समूह Cl के ऑर्थो तथा पैरा स्थिति पर हैं, जो मेसेनहाइमर कॉम्प्लेक्स को स्थिरता देते हैं। अतः (D) सर्वाधिक अभिक्रियाशील है।

questions.text: 1º, 2º और 3º ऐल्कोहॉल निर्जलन के प्रति निम्नलिखित क्रम में से किसका अनुसरण करते हैं?
questions.text_english: The dehydration of 1º, 2º and 3º alcohols follows the order:
questions.solution: Dehydration of alcohols proceeds via carbocation intermediates (E1 mechanism). Tertiary carbocations are most stable due to hyperconjugation and inductive effect of three alkyl groups, followed by secondary, and then primary. Therefore, tertiary alcohols dehydrate most easily at the lowest temperature, followed by secondary, then primary. The correct order is 3º > 2º > 1º, which is option (B).
questions.solution_hindi: निर्जलन कार्बधनायन मध्यवर्ती के माध्यम से होता है। तृतीयक कार्बधनायन सर्वाधिक स्थाई होता है, इसलिए तृतीयक ऐल्कोहॉल सबसे आसानी से निर्जलित होते हैं। क्रम: 3º > 2º > 1º। सही उत्तर (B) है।

questions.text: [Co(NH3)5(ONO)] SO4 में Co की ऑक्सीकरण संख्या है:
questions.text_english: The oxidation number of Co in [Co(NH3)5(ONO)] SO4 is:
questions.solution: In [Co(NH3)5(ONO)]SO4, the overall complex cation is [Co(NH3)5(ONO)]2+ and SO4 carries a 2- charge. NH3 is neutral (0), ONO- (nitrito ligand) carries a charge of -1. Let oxidation state of Co be x. Then: x + 5(0) + (-1) = +2, so x - 1 = 2, therefore x = +3. The oxidation number of Co is +3. Option (A) is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: SO4 का आवेश -2 है, इसलिए संकुल आयन का आवेश +2 है। NH3 उदासीन है, ONO- का आवेश -1 है। Co की ऑक्सीकरण संख्या x: x + 0 + (-1) = +2, अतः x = +3। सही उत्तर (A) है।

questions.text: वर्नर के सिद्धांत के अनुसार, केन्द्रीय धातु परमाणु की प्राथमिक संयोजकताएँ:
questions.text_english: According to Werner's theory, the primary valencies of the central metal atom:

options.A: उदासीन अणुओं अथवा ऋणात्मक आयनों द्वारा संतुष्ट होती हैं।
options.B: उपसहसंयोजन संख्या के बराबर होती हैं।
options.C: ऋणात्मक आयनों से संतुष्ट होती हैं।

options_english.A: are satisfied by neutral molecules or negative ions.
options_english.B: are equal to its coordination number.

questions.solution: According to Werner's theory, primary valency corresponds to the oxidation state of the central metal and is always satisfied by negative ions only (anions). It is ionisable. Secondary valency (coordination number) is satisfied by both neutral molecules and negative ions. Option A incorrectly states neutral molecules also satisfy primary valency. Option B confuses primary valency with coordination number. Option D is wrong because primary valency is ionisable. Hence (C) is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: वर्नर के सिद्धांत में, प्राथमिक संयोजकताएँ (ऑक्सीकरण अवस्था) केवल ऋणात्मक आयनों द्वारा संतुष्ट होती हैं और ये आयनशील होती हैं। द्वितीयक संयोजकताएँ (उपसहसंयोजन संख्या) उदासीन अणुओं या ऋणात्मक आयनों से संतुष्ट होती हैं। सही उत्तर (C) है।

questions.text: C2H5NH2 और (C2H5)2NH में विभेद करने के लिए कौन-सा अभिकर्मक प्रयुक्त होता है?
questions.text_english: Which reagent is used to distinguish between C2H5NH2 and (C2H5)2NH?
questions.solution: The carbylamine (isocyanide) test uses CHCl3 and ethanolic KOH and gives a foul-smelling isocyanide only with primary amines (those having at least one N-H bond adjacent to the nitrogen with no substitution). C2H5NH2 is a primary amine and gives a positive carbylamine test (foul smell of ethyl isocyanide), whereas (C2H5)2NH is a secondary amine and does not give this test. Thus CHCl3 + KOH (ethanolic) is the distinguishing reagent. Option (B) is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: कार्बिलेमीन परीक्षण (CHCl3 + KOH एथेनॉलिक) केवल प्राथमिक ऐमीनों के साथ सकारात्मक परिणाम देता है। C2H5NH2 (प्राथमिक) दुर्गंधयुक्त आइसोसाइनाइड देता है, जबकि (C2H5)2NH (द्वितीयक) नहीं देता। सही उत्तर (B) है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किसका pKb मान न्यूनतम है?
questions.text_english: Among the following, which one has the lowest value of pKb?
questions.image_description: Four structural formulas of amines: (A) benzylamine — benzene ring attached to CH2-NH2; (B) 4-methylaniline — benzene ring with NH2 at position 1 and CH3 at position 4; (C) 4-nitroaniline — benzene ring with NH2 at position 1 and NO2 at position 4; (D) aniline — benzene ring with NH2 directly attached.
questions.solution: Lowest pKb means highest basicity (strongest base). Benzylamine (A) is an aliphatic amine where the NH2 is not directly attached to the aromatic ring but is separated by a CH2 group, so lone pair on nitrogen is not delocalised into the ring. It is therefore more basic than any aromatic amine. Among aromatic amines, electron-donating groups increase basicity. The CH3 group in 4-methylaniline (B) increases basicity over aniline (D), while NO2 group in (C) greatly decreases basicity. Therefore, order of basicity: A > B > D > C, so benzylamine has the lowest pKb. Option (A) is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: बेन्जिलेमीन (A) एक ऐलिफैटिक ऐमीन है जिसमें CH2 समूह नाइट्रोजन के एकाकी युग्म को ऐरोमैटिक वलय से अलग करता है। इसलिए यह ऐनिलीन और अन्य ऐरोमैटिक ऐमीनों से अधिक क्षारीय है। न्यूनतम pKb = अधिकतम क्षारकता। सही उत्तर (A) है।

questions.text: जलीय अम्लीय विलयन में, CrO4^2- आयन निम्नलिखित में से किसमें रूपान्तरित हो जाता है?
questions.text_english: In aqueous acidified solution, CrO4^2- ion converts to which of the following?
questions.solution: Chromate ion (CrO4^2-, yellow) is stable in alkaline or neutral solution. When acidified, two chromate ions condense to form dichromate ion: 2CrO4^2- + 2H+ → Cr2O7^2- + H2O. The solution turns from yellow to orange. CrO3 and Cr3+ require further reactions or strong reducing agents, and CrO does not form under these conditions. Therefore, option (C) Cr2O7^2- is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: क्रोमेट आयन (CrO4^2-, पीला) अम्लीय विलयन में डाइक्रोमेट आयन (Cr2O7^2-, नारंगी) में परिवर्तित हो जाता है: 2CrO4^2- + 2H+ → Cr2O7^2- + H2O। सही उत्तर (C) है।

questions.text: शुद्ध जल और नाइट्रिक अम्ल के क्वथनांकों की अपेक्षा जल और नाइट्रिक अम्ल के स्थिरक्वाथी मिश्रण का क्वथनांक अधिक होता है। यह मिश्रण दर्शाता है:
questions.text_english: The boiling point of an azeotropic mixture of water and nitric acid is more than that of pure water and nitric acid. The mixture shows:

options.B: that solution is an ideal solution

options_english.B: that solution is an ideal solution

questions.solution: A solution that has a higher boiling point than either of its pure components forms a maximum boiling azeotrope. This occurs when intermolecular interactions between unlike molecules (A-B) are stronger than those between like molecules (A-A and B-B), resulting in a lower vapour pressure than expected — this is negative deviation from Raoult's law. Water and nitric acid interact strongly (due to hydrogen bonding and ion-dipole interactions), so the mixture shows negative deviation from Raoult's law. Option (D) is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: स्थिरक्वाथी मिश्रण का क्वथनांक घटकों से अधिक होने पर उच्चतम क्वथनांक ऐज़ियोट्रोप बनता है, जो राउल्ट के नियम से ऋणात्मक विचलन दर्शाता है। जल-नाइट्रिक अम्ल के बीच प्रबल अंतराण्विक आकर्षण होता है। सही उत्तर (D) है।

questions.text: जल-अपघटन होने पर, निम्नलिखित काबोहाइड्रेटों में से कौन-सा केवल ग्लूकोस देता है?
questions.text_english: On hydrolysis, which of the following carbohydrates gives only glucose?
questions.solution: Starch is a polysaccharide made entirely of glucose units (both amylose and amylopectin are composed of alpha-D-glucose). On hydrolysis, starch gives only glucose. Sucrose gives glucose and fructose. Lactose gives glucose and galactose. Galactose is a monosaccharide and does not undergo hydrolysis to give glucose. Therefore, option (A) Starch is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: स्टार्च पूर्णतः ग्लूकोस इकाइयों से बना बहुलक है। इसके जल-अपघटन से केवल ग्लूकोस प्राप्त होता है। सुक्रोस से ग्लूकोस + फ्रक्टोस और लैक्टोस से ग्लूकोस + गैलेक्टोस मिलता है। सही उत्तर (A) है।

questions.text: अभिक्रिया 2A → 3B के लिए, अभिक्रिया वेग +d[B]/dt बराबर है:
questions.text_english: For the reaction 2A → 3B, the rate of reaction +d[B]/dt is equal to:
questions.solution: For the reaction 2A → 3B, the rate of reaction is expressed as: Rate = -(1/2) d[A]/dt = +(1/3) d[B]/dt. Therefore, d[B]/dt = (3/2) × (-(d[A]/dt)) = -(3/2) d[A]/dt. Since A is being consumed, d[A]/dt is negative, making the overall expression positive, which is consistent. Option (A) is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: अभिक्रिया 2A → 3B के लिए: -(1/2)d[A]/dt = +(1/3)d[B]/dt। अतः +d[B]/dt = -(3/2)d[A]/dt। सही उत्तर (A) है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : Zr और Hf का पृथक्करण कठिन होता है।
कारण (R) : लैन्थेनॉयड आकुंचन के कारण Zr और Hf की परमाणु एवं आयनिक त्रिज्याएँ लगभग समान होती हैं।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Separation of Zr and Hf is difficult.
Reason (R) : Zr and Hf have almost identical atomic and ionic radii due to lanthanoid contraction.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Zirconium (Zr, Period 5) and Hafnium (Hf, Period 6) belong to the same group (Group 4). Due to lanthanoid contraction, the expected increase in atomic and ionic radii from Zr to Hf is cancelled out, making their radii nearly identical (Zr: 160 pm, Hf: 159 pm). Because of this near-identical size and similar chemical properties, separating Zr and Hf is extremely difficult. Both the assertion and reason are correct, and the reason correctly explains the assertion. Option (A) is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: लैन्थेनॉयड आकुंचन के कारण Zr और Hf की परमाणु व आयनिक त्रिज्याएँ लगभग बराबर हो जाती हैं, जिसके कारण उनके रासायनिक गुण भी समान होते हैं और पृथक्करण कठिन होता है। अभिकथन और कारण दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण सही व्याख्या है। सही उत्तर (A) है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : 4-मेथिलफीनॉल की तुलना में फीनॉल अधिक अम्लीय होती है।
कारण (R) : फीनॉल में इलेक्ट्रॉन विमोचक समूह की उपस्थिति उसे अधिक अम्लीय बना देता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Phenol is more acidic than 4-methylphenol.
Reason (R) : The presence of an electron releasing group in phenol makes it more acidic.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.C: A is true but R is false.
options.D: A is false but R is true.

options_english.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options_english.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options_english.C: A is true but R is false.
options_english.D: A is false but R is true.

questions.solution: The assertion is true: phenol is more acidic than 4-methylphenol because the methyl group in 4-methylphenol is electron-donating (via hyperconjugation/inductive effect), which increases the electron density on oxygen, making it harder to release the proton, thus decreasing acidity. The reason, however, is false — it incorrectly states that the electron-releasing group in phenol makes it more acidic. In reality, it is the absence of any substituent in phenol (compared to the electron-donating methyl in 4-methylphenol) that makes phenol more acidic. An electron-releasing group decreases acidity, not increases it. Therefore option (C) is correct: A is true, R is false.
questions.solution_hindi: अभिकथन सत्य है — फीनॉल, 4-मेथिलफीनॉल से अधिक अम्लीय है क्योंकि मेथिल समूह इलेक्ट्रॉन देने वाला है जो अम्लता घटाता है। कारण गलत है — इलेक्ट्रॉन विमोचक समूह अम्लता को बढ़ाता नहीं, घटाता है। सही उत्तर (C) है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : ऐरोमैटिक प्राथमिक ऐमीनों को गैब्रिएल थैलिमाइड संश्लेषण द्वारा आसानी से बनाया जा सकता है।
कारण (R) : गैब्रिएल थैलिमाइड संश्लेषण केवल ऐलिफैटिक प्राथमिक ऐमीनों को बनाने के लिए प्रयुक्त की जाती है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Aromatic primary amines can easily be prepared by Gabriel phthalimide synthesis.
Reason (R) : Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used to prepare only aliphatic primary amines.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.C: A is true but R is false.
options.D: A is false but R is true.

options_english.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options_english.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options_english.C: A is true but R is false.
options_english.D: A is false but R is true.

questions.solution: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis involves the alkylation of potassium phthalimide with an alkyl halide, followed by hydrolysis to yield a primary amine. Since aryl halides do not readily undergo nucleophilic substitution under these mild conditions, aromatic primary amines cannot be prepared by this method. Thus the assertion (A) is false. The reason (R) is correct — Gabriel synthesis is used only for aliphatic primary amines. Therefore option (D) is correct: A is false, R is true.
questions.solution_hindi: गैब्रिएल संश्लेषण में ऐरिल हैलाइड नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन नहीं देते, इसलिए ऐरोमैटिक प्राथमिक ऐमीन नहीं बन सकती। अतः अभिकथन (A) गलत है। कारण (R) सही है — यह विधि केवल ऐलिफैटिक प्राथमिक ऐमीनों के लिए है। सही उत्तर (D) है।

कारण (R) : अभिक्रिया की कोटि एक प्रायोगिक मात्रा है।

Assertion (A) : Order of reaction is not applicable for elementary reaction but applicable for complex reaction.
Reason (R) : Order of reaction is an experimental quantity.

options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.C: A is true but R is false.
options.D: A is false but R is true.

options_english.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options_english.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options_english.C: A is true but R is false.
options_english.D: A is false but R is true.

questions.solution: The assertion (A) is false. Order of reaction is applicable to both elementary and complex reactions. For elementary reactions, the order equals the molecularity and can be determined from stoichiometry. For complex reactions, order is determined experimentally and may be fractional or zero. The reason (R) is true — order is indeed an experimentally determined quantity. Hence option (D) is correct: A is false, R is true.

questions.text: व्याख्या कीजिए कि क्यों 1 लीटर जल में 1 मोल KCl मिलाने पर जल का क्वथनांक बढ़ जाता है, जबकि 1 लीटर जल में 1 मोल मेथिल ऐल्कोहॉल मिलाने पर जल का क्वथनांक घट जाता है।
questions.text_english: Explain why, on addition of 1 mol of KCl to 1 litre of water, the boiling point of water increases, while the addition of 1 mol of methyl alcohol to 1 litre of water decreases the boiling point.

key_points: KCl is an electrolyte that dissociates into 2 ions (K+ and Cl-), increasing the total number of solute particles, which raises the boiling point (elevation of boiling point is a colligative property).
Methyl alcohol is volatile and miscible with water; it increases the vapour pressure of the solution (positive deviation from Raoult's law), which lowers the boiling point.

questions.solution: KCl is a strong electrolyte that completely dissociates in water into K+ and Cl- ions, giving two moles of solute particles per mole dissolved. This increases the total concentration of solute particles, reducing the vapour pressure and thus elevating the boiling point (ΔTb = Kb × m × i). Methyl alcohol (methanol), on the other hand, is a volatile liquid that is completely miscible with water. When added to water, it increases the vapour pressure of the solution beyond what is expected (positive deviation from Raoult's law), which results in a decrease in the boiling point of the solution.
questions.solution_hindi: KCl प्रबल विद्युत-अपघट्य है जो K+ और Cl- में पूर्णतः वियोजित होता है, जिससे विलेय कणों की संख्या बढ़ती है और क्वथनांक उन्नयन होता है। मेथिल ऐल्कोहॉल वाष्पशील द्रव है जो जल के साथ मिलकर राउल्ट के नियम से धनात्मक विचलन दर्शाता है, जिससे वाष्प दाब बढ़ता है और क्वथनांक घटता है।

sub_questions.text_english: Define ambidentate ligand with an example.

key_points: A ligand that can donate a lone pair from two different donor atoms is called an ambidentate ligand. Example: NO2- can coordinate through N (nitro) or through O (nitrito).

sub_questions.solution: An ambidentate ligand is one that can bind to the central metal atom through two different donor atoms. For example, the nitrite ion (NO2-) can coordinate through its nitrogen atom (giving the nitro linkage, -NO2) or through an oxygen atom (giving the nitrito linkage, -ONO). Another example is thiocyanate (SCN-) which can bond via S or N.

sub_questions.text_english: Define double salt with an example.

key_points: A double salt is formed by the combination of two simple salts and dissociates completely in solution to give all constituent ions. Example: Mohr's salt, FeSO4.(NH4)2SO4.6H2O.

sub_questions.solution: A double salt is a salt that is formed by the crystallisation of two different ionic compounds together and completely dissociates in aqueous solution to give all constituent ions. For example, Mohr's salt [FeSO4·(NH4)2SO4·6H2O] is a double salt that dissociates in solution to give Fe2+, NH4+, and SO4^2- ions freely.

key_points: (i) Ambidentate ligand: can donate lone pair from two different atoms. Example: NO2- (nitro via N, nitrito via O).
(ii) Double salt: formed by combination of two simple salts, dissociates completely in solution. Example: Mohr's salt.

questions.solution: (i) An ambidentate ligand can bind to the central metal through two different donor atoms. The nitrite ion (NO2-) is a classic example — it can coordinate via nitrogen (nitro, -NO2) or via oxygen (nitrito, -ONO). (ii) A double salt results from the combination of two simple salts and upon dissolution in water, all constituent ions are released freely. Mohr's salt (FeSO4·(NH4)2SO4·6H2O) is a well-known example, giving Fe2+, NH4+, and SO4^2- ions in solution.

(क) समावयव जो SN1 प्रतिस्थापन के प्रति सर्वाधिक अभिक्रियाशील है।

questions.text_english:
For the compound having molecular formula C4H9Br, write:
(a) the isomer which is most reactive towards SN1 displacement.
(b) the isomer which, on reacting with Na metal in the presence of dry ether, gives 2,5-Dimethylhexane.

sub_questions.text: C4H9Br का वह समावयव जो SN1 प्रतिस्थापन के प्रति सर्वाधिक अभिक्रियाशील है।
sub_questions.text_english: The isomer of C4H9Br most reactive towards SN1 displacement.

key_points: (CH3)3CBr — tert-butyl bromide (2-bromo-2-methylpropane)

sub_questions.solution: SN1 reactivity depends on the stability of the carbocation formed. Among the isomers of C4H9Br, (CH3)3CBr (tert-butyl bromide) forms the most stable tertiary carbocation upon ionisation, making it the most reactive towards SN1 substitution.

sub_questions.text: C4H9Br का वह समावयव जो शुष्क ईथर में Na के साथ 2,5-डाइमेथिलहैक्सेन देता है।

key_points: (CH3)2CHCH2Br — isobutyl bromide (2-methylpropyl bromide / 1-bromo-2-methylpropane)

sub_questions.solution: Wurtz reaction: 2 R-X + 2Na → R-R + 2NaX. 2,5-Dimethylhexane is (CH3)2CHCH2CH2CH(CH3)2, which is formed by coupling two isobutyl groups. So the halide must be isobutyl bromide: (CH3)2CHCH2Br (1-bromo-2-methylpropane). Two moles react with Na in dry ether to give 2,5-dimethylhexane.

key_points: (a) (CH3)3CBr — tert-butyl bromide, most reactive in SN1.
(b) (CH3)2CHCH2Br — isobutyl bromide, gives 2,5-dimethylhexane via Wurtz reaction.

questions.solution: (a) The isomer most reactive towards SN1 is (CH3)3CBr (tert-butyl bromide / 2-bromo-2-methylpropane) because it produces the most stable tertiary carbocation intermediate. (b) For the Wurtz reaction with Na in dry ether: 2 (CH3)2CHCH2Br + 2Na → (CH3)2CHCH2CH2CH(CH3)2 + 2NaBr. The product 2,5-dimethylhexane is formed by joining two isobutyl groups, so the required isomer is isobutyl bromide: (CH3)2CHCH2Br (1-bromo-2-methylpropane).

अभिक्रिया A + B → उत्पाद के लिए, वेग नियम है:
वेग = k[A][B]^(3/2)
अभिक्रिया की समग्र कोटि लिखिए। क्या यह अभिक्रिया एक प्राथमिक अभिक्रिया हो सकती है? अपने उत्तर के समर्थन के लिए कारण दीजिए।
questions.text_english:
For a reaction A + B → Products, the rate law is:
Rate = k[A][B]^(3/2)
Write the overall order of the reaction. Can this reaction be an elementary reaction? Give reason in support of your answer.

key_points: Overall order = 1 + 3/2 = 5/2 (2.5)
No, it cannot be an elementary reaction because the order with respect to B is 3/2 (a fraction), and elementary reactions can only have whole number orders equal to stoichiometric coefficients.

questions.solution: The overall order of the reaction is obtained by adding the powers of concentration terms in the rate law: order = 1 (for A) + 3/2 (for B) = 5/2 = 2.5. This reaction cannot be an elementary reaction because for an elementary reaction, the order must be a whole number equal to the stoichiometric coefficient of each reactant (i.e., the order must be 1 for A and 1 for B as per A + B → Products). A fractional order of 3/2 with respect to B indicates that the reaction proceeds through a complex multi-step mechanism.
questions.solution_hindi: समग्र कोटि = 1 + 3/2 = 5/2 = 2.5। यह प्राथमिक अभिक्रिया नहीं हो सकती क्योंकि प्राथमिक अभिक्रिया में कोटि केवल पूर्ण संख्या (stoichiometric coefficient के बराबर) होती है। B के प्रति भिन्नात्मक कोटि 3/2 दर्शाता है कि यह बहुपदीय जटिल अभिक्रिया है।

questions.text_english:
How do you explain the following?
(a) Presence of a carbonyl group in glucose
(b) Presence of five – OH groups in glucose

sub_questions.text: ग्लूकोस में कार्बोनिल समूह की उपस्थिति की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the presence of a carbonyl group in glucose.

key_points: Glucose reacts with hydroxylamine to form an oxime and with HCN to give a cyanohydrin, indicating the presence of an aldehyde (carbonyl) group.

sub_questions.solution: The presence of an aldehyde carbonyl group in glucose is evidenced by the following: glucose reacts with hydroxylamine (NH2OH) to form a crystalline oxime (glucose oxime), and with HCN to give a cyanohydrin. It also reduces Tollens' reagent (gives silver mirror) and Fehling's solution (gives red precipitate), which are characteristic reactions of aldehydes.

sub_questions.text: ग्लूकोस में पाँच – OH समूहों की उपस्थिति की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the presence of five – OH groups in glucose.

key_points: Glucose reacts with 5 moles of acetic anhydride to form glucose pentaacetate, indicating the presence of five -OH groups.

sub_questions.solution: The presence of five hydroxyl (-OH) groups in glucose is demonstrated by the fact that glucose reacts with acetic anhydride (CH3CO)2O to form glucose pentaacetate. Since one mole of glucose reacts with five moles of acetic anhydride, this confirms the presence of five -OH groups in the glucose molecule.

key_points: (a) Glucose forms oxime with NH2OH and cyanohydrin with HCN; reduces Tollens' and Fehling's reagent — confirms carbonyl (aldehyde) group.
(b) Glucose reacts with 5 moles of acetic anhydride to give glucose pentaacetate — confirms five -OH groups.

questions.solution: (a) The carbonyl group in glucose is an aldehyde at C-1. Evidence: glucose reacts with hydroxylamine to form an oxime and reduces Tollens' reagent (silver mirror test) and Fehling's solution (brick-red precipitate), which are characteristic of aldehydes. (b) When glucose is treated with excess acetic anhydride, it forms glucose pentaacetate, meaning five acetyl groups are attached — this confirms that glucose contains five free hydroxyl (-OH) groups.

निम्नलिखित के लिए कारण दीजिए:
(क) ऐल्किल हैलाइड यद्यपि ध्रुवीय होते हैं, फिर भी उनकी जल में विलेयता बहुत कम होती है।
(ख) ऑर्थो- और मेटा-समावयवों की अपेक्षा p-डाइक्लोरोबेन्जीन का गलनांक उच्चतर होता है।
(ग) SN2 अभिक्रियाओं के प्रति CH3 – Br की तुलना में CH3 – I अधिक अभिक्रियाशील होता है।
questions.text_english:
Give reasons for the following:
(a) Alkyl halides, though polar, yet their solubility in water is very low.
(b) p-Dichlorobenzene has higher melting point than those of o- and m-isomers.
(c) CH3 – I is more reactive than CH3 – Br towards SN2 reactions.

key_points: (a) Alkyl halides cannot form hydrogen bonds with water to overcome the energy needed to break the strong H-bonding network of water; hence low solubility.
(b) p-Dichlorobenzene has a symmetrical structure, allowing better packing in crystal lattice, resulting in a higher melting point.
(c) In SN2, the rate depends on the leaving group ability. I- is a better leaving group than Br- (weaker C-I bond, more polarisable), so CH3-I reacts faster.

questions.solution: (a) Although alkyl halides are polar (due to the C-X bond), they cannot form hydrogen bonds with water molecules because they lack an O-H or N-H bond. To dissolve in water, the strong hydrogen bonding network of water must be broken, requiring significant energy that is not compensated by the weak interactions between water and alkyl halide molecules. Hence, alkyl halides have very low solubility in water. (b) p-Dichlorobenzene has a symmetrical structure (Cl atoms at opposite ends of the ring), which allows for more efficient close packing of molecules in the crystalline lattice. This symmetrical packing results in stronger intermolecular forces and a higher melting point compared to o- and m-isomers, which are less symmetrical and pack less efficiently. (c) In SN2 reactions, the rate depends on the ease with which the leaving group departs. Iodide (I-) is a better leaving group than bromide (Br-) because the C-I bond is longer and weaker (bond enthalpy: C-I < C-Br), and iodide ion is more stable as a leaving group due to its larger size and higher polarisability. Therefore, CH3-I reacts faster than CH3-Br in SN2 reactions.

(क) फीनॉल
(ख) आयोडोबेन्जीन

questions.text_english:
How will you obtain the following from benzene diazonium chloride? Write chemical equations involved:
(a) Phenol
(b) Iodobenzene
(c) p-Aminoazobenzene

key_points: (a) Phenol: Benzene diazonium chloride is heated with water (hydrolysis). C6H5N2+Cl- + H2O → C6H5OH + N2 + HCl
(b) Iodobenzene: Sandmeyer reaction with KI. C6H5N2+Cl- + KI → C6H5I + N2 + KCl
(c) p-Aminoazobenzene: Coupling reaction with aniline in weakly acidic medium. C6H5N2+Cl- + C6H5NH2 → p-H2N-C6H4-N=N-C6H5 + HCl

questions.solution: (a) Phenol is obtained by warming benzene diazonium chloride with water (or by steam distillation): C6H5N2+Cl- + H2O → C6H5OH + N2↑ + HCl. (b) Iodobenzene is prepared by Sandmeyer reaction — treating benzene diazonium chloride with potassium iodide (KI): C6H5N2+Cl- + KI → C6H5I + N2↑ + KCl. (c) p-Aminoazobenzene (an azo dye) is prepared by the coupling reaction of benzene diazonium chloride with aniline in weakly acidic (acetic acid) medium. The electrophilic diazonium ion attacks the para position of aniline (which is activated by the -NH2 group): C6H5N2+Cl- + C6H5NH2 → p-H2N-C6H4-N=N-C6H5 + HCl.

questions.text: C3H5N आण्विक सूत्र का एक कार्बनिक यौगिक (A), C6H5MgBr के साथ अभिक्रिया करने के उपरान्त जल-अपघटन करने पर यौगिक (B) देता है। यौगिक (B), 2,4-डी.एन.पी. अभिकर्मक के साथ नारंगी-लाल अवक्षेप देता है तथा आयोडोफॉर्म परीक्षण नहीं देता है। यह टॉलेन्स अभिकर्मक अथवा फेलिंग अभिकर्मक को अपचित नहीं करता है और न ही ब्रोमीन जल को वर्णाविहीन करता है। यह क्रोमिक अम्ल द्वारा प्रबल ऑक्सीकरण से एक कार्बोक्सिलिक अम्ल (C) बनाता है जिसका आण्विक सूत्र C7H6O2 है। यौगिक (A), (B) और (C) को पहचानिए। यौगिक (A) की C6H5MgBr के साथ अभिक्रिया करने के उपरान्त जल-अपघटन करने पर यौगिक (B) बनने की अभिक्रियाएँ लिखिए।
questions.text_english: An organic compound (A) with molecular formula C3H5N on reaction with C6H5MgBr followed by hydrolysis, gives a compound (B). Compound (B) forms an orange-red precipitate with 2,4-DNP reagent and does not give iodoform test. It neither reduces Tollens' or Fehling's reagent nor does it decolourise bromine water. On drastic oxidation with chromic acid it gives a carboxylic acid (C) having molecular formula C7H6O2. Identify the compounds (A), (B) and (C). Write the reactions of compound (A) with C6H5MgBr followed by hydrolysis to give compound (B).

key_points: A = CH3CN (methyl cyanide / acetonitrile)
B = C6H5COCH3 (acetophenone / methyl phenyl ketone)
C = C6H5COOH (benzoic acid)
Reaction: CH3CN + C6H5MgBr → CH3C(=NMgBr)C6H5 → [H3O+] → CH3COC6H5 (acetophenone)

questions.solution: Compound (A) has molecular formula C3H5N. With C6H5MgBr (Grignard reagent) followed by hydrolysis, it gives (B) which gives orange-red precipitate with 2,4-DNP (indicating ketone or aldehyde), does NOT give iodoform test (ruling out methyl ketone CH3CO- ... but wait, acetophenone is indeed a methyl ketone yet does not give iodoform — actually acetophenone DOES give iodoform). Let us reconsider: compound B does not give iodoform, does not reduce Tollens' or Fehling's (rules out aldehyde), does not decolourise bromine water (no C=C). On drastic oxidation with chromic acid gives C7H6O2 (benzoic acid, C6H5COOH). If B gives benzoic acid on oxidation, B must contain a C6H5 group attached to a carbonyl. B is a ketone (gives 2,4-DNP but not Tollens'/Fehling'). Given A is C3H5N: A = CH2=CH-CN (acrylonitrile) or CH3CN (acetonitrile). If A = CH3CN, then A + C6H5MgBr gives addition to CN, followed by hydrolysis: CH3CN + C6H5MgBr → imine salt → H3O+ → CH3COC6H5 (acetophenone). Acetophenone (B) gives 2,4-DNP (ketone), does not reduce Tollens'/Fehling' (not aldehyde), does not give iodoform (incorrect — actually acetophenone DOES give iodoform since it has CH3CO group). Therefore B cannot be acetophenone if it does not give iodoform. Re-examining: if B does not give iodoform, B is C6H5-CO-C2H5 (phenyl ethyl ketone, propiophenone). For that, A must be C2H5CN (propionitrile, C3H5N fits: MW=55). A = CH3CH2CN (propionitrile). A + C6H5MgBr → C6H5C(=NMgBr)C2H5 → H3O+ → C6H5COC2H5 (propiophenone / phenyl ethyl ketone, B). B gives 2,4-DNP (ketone ✓), no iodoform (not methyl ketone ✓), no Tollens'/Fehling' (not aldehyde ✓), no bromine decolouration (no unsaturation ✓). On chromic acid oxidation: C6H5COC2H5 → C6H5COOH (benzoic acid, C7H6O2 ✓). Therefore: A = CH3CH2CN (propionitrile), B = C6H5COC2H5 (propiophenone), C = C6H5COOH (benzoic acid). Reaction: CH3CH2CN + C6H5MgBr → [C6H5C(=NMgBr)CH2CH3] → H3O+/H2O → C6H5COCH2CH3 + NH3.

questions.text_english: An antifreeze solution is prepared by dissolving 31 g of ethylene glycol (Molar mass = 62 g mol^-1) in 600 g of water. Calculate the freezing point of the solution. (Kf for water = 1.86 K kg mol^-1)

key_points: Moles of ethylene glycol = 31/62 = 0.5 mol
Molality m = 0.5 / 0.600 = 0.833 mol/kg
Freezing point = 0 - 1.55 = -1.55°C

questions.solution: Number of moles of ethylene glycol = 31 g ÷ 62 g mol⁻¹ = 0.5 mol. Mass of solvent (water) = 600 g = 0.600 kg. Molality (m) = moles of solute / mass of solvent in kg = 0.5 / 0.600 = 0.833 mol kg⁻¹. Depression in freezing point: ΔTf = Kf × m = 1.86 × 0.833 = 1.55 K. Since the normal freezing point of water is 0°C, the freezing point of the solution = 0 − 1.55 = −1.55°C.

(a) Answer the following questions about the complexes [NiCl4]^2- and [Ni(CN)4]^2-:
(i) Write the hybridization involved in each case.
(ii) Which of them is the inner orbital complex and which one is the outer orbital complex?
(iii) Compare their magnetic behaviour.

key_points: [NiCl4]^2-: sp3 hybridisation, outer orbital complex, paramagnetic (2 unpaired electrons).
[Ni(CN)4]^2-: dsp2 hybridisation, inner orbital complex, diamagnetic (0 unpaired electrons).

questions.solution: Ni has atomic number 28; electronic configuration: [Ar] 3d8 4s2. In complexes, Ni2+ has configuration 3d8. (i) [NiCl4]^2-: Cl- is a weak field ligand and does not cause pairing of electrons. Ni2+ has two unpaired electrons in 3d. Hybridisation is sp3 (uses 4s and 4p orbitals), giving a tetrahedral geometry. [Ni(CN)4]^2-: CN- is a strong field ligand and forces pairing of 3d electrons. All 3d electrons pair up, leaving one empty 3d orbital. Hybridisation is dsp2 (uses one 3d, one 4s, two 4p orbitals), giving a square planar geometry. (ii) [Ni(CN)4]^2- is the inner orbital complex because it uses the inner 3d orbital in hybridisation (dsp2). [NiCl4]^2- is the outer orbital complex because it uses 4s and 4p orbitals only (sp3). (iii) [NiCl4]^2- has two unpaired electrons (from 3d8 in weak field) and is paramagnetic. [Ni(CN)4]^2- has no unpaired electrons (strong field CN- causes pairing) and is diamagnetic.

(ii) What is meant by chelate effect? Give an example.
(iii) Why are low spin tetrahedral complexes rarely formed?

(ii) The chelate effect refers to the enhanced stability of a complex containing chelate rings (formed by polydentate ligands) compared to a similar complex with monodentate ligands. Example: [Co(en)3]^3+ is more stable than [Co(NH3)6]^3+.

questions.solution: (i) Two coordination compounds important in biological systems are haemoglobin (an iron-porphyrin complex that carries oxygen in blood) and chlorophyll (a magnesium-porphyrin complex involved in photosynthesis). (ii) The chelate effect refers to the greater stability of chelate complexes — complexes formed when a polydentate (chelating) ligand forms multiple bonds with a single metal ion, creating ring structures — compared to analogous complexes with monodentate ligands. For example, [Co(en)3]^3+ (where en = ethane-1,2-diamine, a bidentate ligand) is significantly more stable than [Co(NH3)6]^3+. (iii) In tetrahedral complexes, the crystal field splitting energy (Δt) is only 4/9 of the octahedral splitting energy (Δo). This small splitting is generally less than the electron pairing energy, meaning it is energetically unfavourable to force electrons to pair up. Therefore, tetrahedral complexes are almost always high spin, and low spin tetrahedral complexes are rarely observed.

questions.text_english: State Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions. With the help of a curve, explain why it is not easy to determine Λ°m for weak electrolytes by extrapolating the concentration – molar conductivity curve, as it is for strong electrolytes.

key_points: Kohlrausch's Law: At infinite dilution, each ion migrates independently; Λ°m = ν+ λ°+ + ν- λ°-.
For strong electrolytes, Λm vs √C is nearly linear at low concentrations; extrapolation to C=0 gives Λ°m.
For weak electrolytes, Λm rises steeply as concentration approaches zero (due to increasing degree of dissociation); the curve is not linear and cannot be extrapolated reliably.

questions.image_description: A graph with Molar conductivity (Λm) on Y-axis and √C on X-axis. Two curves: one for strong electrolyte (HCl) — nearly linear, can be extrapolated to give Λ°m at C=0; one for weak electrolyte (CH3COOH) — steeply rising curve near C=0 that cannot be reliably extrapolated to determine Λ°m.
questions.solution: Kohlrausch's Law of Independent Migration of Ions states that at infinite dilution, each ion makes a definite contribution to the total molar conductivity of the electrolyte, irrespective of the nature of the other ion present. Mathematically: Λ°m = ν+ λ°+ + ν- λ°-, where ν+ and ν- are the number of cations and anions per formula unit, and λ°+ and λ°- are their limiting molar conductivities. For strong electrolytes, Λm decreases slightly and linearly with increasing √C (Debye-Hückel-Onsager equation). This linear relationship can be extrapolated to √C = 0 to determine Λ°m with reasonable accuracy. For weak electrolytes (e.g., acetic acid), the degree of dissociation is very low at high concentrations but increases rapidly as concentration decreases (approaching infinite dilution). Therefore, the Λm versus √C curve rises very steeply near the origin. This steep, non-linear rise makes reliable extrapolation to zero concentration impossible, so Λ°m cannot be determined graphically for weak electrolytes.

questions.text_english: Living systems are made up of various complex biomolecules like carbohydrates, proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, etc. Proteins and carbohydrates are essential constituents of our food. In addition, some simple molecules like vitamins and mineral salts also play an important role in the functions of organisms. All proteins are polymers of alpha-amino acids. Proteins can be classified into two types on the basis of their molecular shape — Fibrous and Globular proteins. Vitamins are accessory food factors required in the diet. They are classified as fat-soluble and water-soluble. Deficiency of vitamins leads to many diseases. Nucleic acids are the polymers of nucleotides which in turn consist of a base, a pentose sugar and phosphate moiety. There are two types of nucleic acids — DNA and RNA. Nucleic acids are responsible for the transfer of characters from parents to offsprings.

sub_questions.text_english: Write the name of basic building units of proteins and nucleic acids. How can you differentiate between Fibrous and Globular proteins on the basis of their structures?

key_points: Building units: proteins — alpha-amino acids; nucleic acids — nucleotides.
Fibrous proteins: polypeptide chains are elongated/linear, held together by hydrogen bonds in parallel; insoluble in water; example: keratin, collagen.
Globular proteins: polypeptide chains are folded into compact spherical shapes; usually soluble in water; example: haemoglobin, insulin.

sub_questions.solution: The basic building units of proteins are alpha-amino acids, linked together by peptide bonds to form polypeptide chains. The basic building units of nucleic acids are nucleotides, each consisting of a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar, and a phosphate group. Fibrous proteins have polypeptide chains arranged in long parallel strands or sheets held together by hydrogen bonds and disulphide bonds; they are generally insoluble in water (e.g., keratin, collagen). Globular proteins have polypeptide chains coiled and folded into a compact spherical or ellipsoidal shape; they are generally soluble in water and are biologically active (e.g., haemoglobin, insulin).

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Calculate the electrode potential of a half-cell for zinc electrode dipping in 0.01 M ZnSO4 solution at 25°C.
Given: E°(Zn2+/Zn) = −0.76 V, [log 10 = 1]
(ii) Write anode, cathode and overall reaction involved in dry cell.
(iii) Equilibrium constant (Kc) is related to E°cell, but not to Ecell. Why?

key_points: (ii) Anode: Zn → Zn2+ + 2e-; Cathode: MnO2 + NH4+ + e- → MnO(OH) + NH3; Overall: Zn + 2MnO2 + 2NH4Cl → ZnCl2 + 2MnO(OH) + 2NH3
(iii) Kc is related to ΔG° (standard conditions), which relates to E°cell; actual Ecell depends on concentrations and is not constant, so Kc relates to E°cell not Ecell.

questions.solution:
(i) Using the Nernst equation for the half-cell Zn2+(aq) + 2e- → Zn(s):
E = E° - (0.0591/n) × log[1/[Zn2+]]
E = -0.76 - (0.0591/2) × log(1/0.01)
E = -0.76 - (0.02955) × log(100)
E = -0.76 - 0.02955 × 2 = -0.76 - 0.0591 = -0.8191 V ≈ -0.82 V.

(ii) In a dry cell (Leclanche cell):
Anode reaction (oxidation): Zn(s) → Zn2+(aq) + 2e-
Cathode reaction (reduction): 2MnO2(s) + 2NH4+(aq) + 2e- → Mn2O3(s) + 2NH3(g) + H2O(l)
Overall reaction: Zn(s) + 2MnO2(s) + 2NH4Cl(aq) → ZnCl2(aq) + Mn2O3(s) + 2NH3(g) + H2O(l)

(iii) The equilibrium constant Kc is related to the standard Gibbs free energy change: ΔG° = -nFE°cell = -RT ln Kc. E°cell is a constant at a given temperature (measured at standard conditions: all concentrations = 1 M). However, Ecell varies with the concentrations of ions in solution (as given by the Nernst equation). At equilibrium, Ecell = 0 and Kc represents the equilibrium concentrations. Since Kc is fixed at a given temperature and corresponds to ΔG° (not ΔG), it is related to E°cell (constant) but not to Ecell (which changes with concentration).

(ख) (i) 0.001 M ऐसीटिक अम्ल विलयन की चालकता 3.905 × 10^-5 S cm^-1 है। इसकी मोलर चालकता एवं वियोजन मात्रा (α) परिकलित कीजिए।
दिया गया है: λ°(CH3COO-) = 40.9 S cm2 mol^-1, λ°(H+) = 349.6 S cm2 mol^-1
(ii) निम्नलिखित के लिए कारण दीजिए:
(I) मक्यूरी सेल अपनी संपूर्ण कार्य अवधि में स्थिर वोल्टता क्यों प्रदान करता है?

questions.text_english:
(b) (i) The conductivity of 0.001 M solution of acetic acid is 3.905×10^-5 S cm^-1. Calculate its molar conductivity and degree of dissociation (α).
Given: λ°(CH3COO-) = 40.9 S cm2 mol^-1, λ°(H+) = 349.6 S cm2 mol^-1
(ii) Give reasons for the following:
(I) Why does a mercury cell deliver a constant voltage for its entire life?
(II) Why is it necessary to use salt bridge in a galvanic cell?

key_points: (I) Mercury cell: reaction does not involve ions in solution; Hg/HgO electrodes maintain constant composition, so EMF stays constant.
(II) Salt bridge maintains electrical neutrality by allowing ion flow between two half-cells, completing the circuit.

questions.solution:
(i) Molar conductivity Λm = (κ × 1000) / M = (3.905 × 10^-5 × 1000) / 0.001 = 39.05 S cm2 mol^-1. Limiting molar conductivity: Λ°m(CH3COOH) = λ°(H+) + λ°(CH3COO-) = 349.6 + 40.9 = 390.5 S cm2 mol^-1. Degree of dissociation: α = Λm / Λ°m = 39.05 / 390.5 = 0.10 = 10%.

(ii)(I) A mercury cell uses the cell reaction: Zn(s) + HgO(s) → ZnO(s) + Hg(l). This reaction does not involve any ions in solution (electrolyte is a paste of KOH/ZnO and does not change its composition during discharge). Since the concentrations of reactants and products remain constant throughout the cell's life, the EMF remains constant (Nernst equation: EMF depends on concentration — no concentration change means constant voltage).

(II) A salt bridge is necessary in a galvanic cell to: (a) complete the electrical circuit by allowing migration of ions between the two half-cells; and (b) maintain electrical neutrality in both half-cell solutions. Without the salt bridge, positive charge would build up in the oxidation half-cell and negative charge in the reduction half-cell, creating a charge imbalance that would stop the cell reaction.

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Describe giving reason which one of the following pairs has the property indicated:
(I) Fe or Cu − higher melting point
(II) Ti3+ or Sc3+ − coloured in aqueous solution
(III) Cr or Zn − higher third ionisation enthalpy
(ii) Write the ionic equations for the oxidizing action of MnO4- in acidic medium with:
(I) Fe2+ ion
(II) I- ion

key_points: (I) Fe has higher melting point; Fe has more unpaired 3d electrons contributing to metallic bonding.
(II) Ti3+ is coloured (3d1 configuration, d-d transition possible); Sc3+ is colourless (3d0, no d electrons for d-d transition).
(III) Zn has higher 3rd ionisation enthalpy; Zn has [Ar]3d10 configuration, removing 3rd electron disrupts stable filled d subshell.
(I ionic eq) MnO4- + 8H+ + 5Fe2+ → Mn2+ + 4H2O + 5Fe3+
(II ionic eq) 2MnO4- + 16H+ + 10I- → 2Mn2+ + 8H2O + 5I2

questions.solution:
(i)(I) Fe has a higher melting point than Cu. Iron (Fe) has the electronic configuration [Ar]3d64s2, with more unpaired 3d electrons (4 unpaired) available for metallic bonding compared to Cu ([Ar]3d104s1, 0 unpaired 3d electrons). Greater number of unpaired electrons leads to stronger metallic bonds, hence higher melting point. Fe: 1535°C; Cu: 1083°C.

(II) Ti3+ is coloured in aqueous solution while Sc3+ is colourless. Ti3+ has configuration [Ar]3d1 — it has one 3d electron which can undergo d-d electronic transition by absorbing visible light, resulting in colour. Sc3+ has configuration [Ar]3d0 — it has no d electrons, so d-d transitions are not possible, and it is colourless.

(III) Zn has a higher third ionisation enthalpy than Cr. Zn has the electronic configuration [Ar]3d104s2. After losing two electrons, Zn2+ has [Ar]3d10 (completely filled d subshell). The third ionisation removes an electron from this stable, completely filled 3d10 configuration, requiring significantly more energy. Cr, after losing two electrons (Cr2+: [Ar]3d4), loses its third electron from a less stable 3d4 configuration, requiring less energy.

(ii)(I) In acidic medium, MnO4- oxidises Fe2+ to Fe3+:
MnO4- + 8H+ + 5e- → Mn2+ + 4H2O (×1)
Fe2+ → Fe3+ + e- (×5)
Net ionic equation: MnO4-(aq) + 8H+(aq) + 5Fe2+(aq) → Mn2+(aq) + 5Fe3+(aq) + 4H2O(l)

(II) In acidic medium, MnO4- oxidises I- to I2:
MnO4- + 8H+ + 5e- → Mn2+ + 4H2O (×2)
2I- → I2 + 2e- (×5)
Net ionic equation: 2MnO4-(aq) + 16H+(aq) + 10I-(aq) → 2Mn2+(aq) + 5I2(s) + 8H2O(l)

(ii) क्या होता है जब हरे रंग के यौगिक (B) के अम्लीय विलयन को कुछ समय के लिए रखा जाता है? सम्मिलित समीकरण भी लिखिए। इस प्रकार की अभिक्रिया को क्या कहा जाता है?
questions.text_english:
(b) (i) A black-brown coloured solid (A) when fused with KOH in the presence of air, produces a dark green coloured compound (B) which on electrolytic oxidation in alkaline medium gives a dark purple coloured compound (C). Identify (A), (B) and (C). Write the reactions involved.
(ii) What happens when an acidic solution of the green compound (B) is allowed to stand for some time? Also write the equation involved. What is this type of reaction called?

key_points: A = MnO2 (manganese dioxide, black-brown solid)
B = K2MnO4 (potassium manganate, dark green)
C = KMnO4 (potassium permanganate, dark purple)
Reaction A→B: 2MnO2 + 4KOH + O2 → 2K2MnO4 + 2H2O
Reaction B→C: electrolytic oxidation in alkaline medium: 2MnO4^2- → MnO4- + e- (at anode)
(ii) In acidic solution, K2MnO4 disproportionates: 3K2MnO4 + 2H2SO4 → 2KMnO4 + MnO2 + 2K2SO4 + 2H2O — this is called disproportionation.

questions.solution:
(i) Compound (A) is MnO2 (manganese dioxide) — a black-brown solid. When fused with KOH in presence of air (oxygen), it undergoes oxidation to give compound (B), dark green K2MnO4 (potassium manganate, Mn in +6 state): 2MnO2 + 4KOH + O2 → 2K2MnO4 + 2H2O. K2MnO4 (B) on electrolytic oxidation in alkaline medium is oxidised at the anode to give compound (C), dark purple KMnO4 (potassium permanganate, Mn in +7 state): 2K2MnO4 → 2KMnO4 + 2e- (at anode) / electrolytic oxidation gives: MnO4^2- - e- → MnO4- Overall: 2MnO4^2-(aq) → 2MnO4-(aq) + 2e-.

(ii) When the acidic solution of green compound B (K2MnO4, potassium manganate) is allowed to stand, it undergoes disproportionation: 3K2MnO4 + 2H2SO4 → 2KMnO4 + MnO2↓ + 2K2SO4 + 2H2O. In this reaction, Mn(+6) in manganate disproportionates — two-thirds is oxidised to Mn(+7) in KMnO4 (purple) and one-third is reduced to Mn(+4) in MnO2 (brown precipitate). This type of reaction is called disproportionation (comproportionation reverse).

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Write the product(s) when:
(I) One mol of ethanal is treated with 1 mol of CH3OH in the presence of dry HCl gas.
(II) Benzaldehyde is treated with conc. NaOH.
(III) Ethanoic acid is heated in the presence of P2O5.
(ii) Write a simple chemical test to distinguish between Ethanal and Propanal.
(iii) Write the name of the reagent to transform Allyl alcohol to Propenal.

key_points: (I) CH3CH(OCH3)2 — dimethyl acetal (acetaldehyde dimethyl acetal) — but with 1 mol CH3OH only hemiacetal CH3CH(OH)(OCH3) is formed.
Actually with 1 mol: CH3CHO + CH3OH → CH3CH(OH)OCH3 (hemiacetal)
(II) Cannizzaro reaction: 2C6H5CHO + NaOH → C6H5COONa + C6H5CH2OH (sodium benzoate + benzyl alcohol)
(III) CH3CO-O-COCH3 (acetic anhydride) from ethanoic acid + P2O5
(ii) Iodoform test: Ethanal gives yellow precipitate of CHI3 with I2/NaOH; Propanal does not.
(iii) MnO2 (manganese dioxide) or PCC to oxidise allyl alcohol (prop-2-en-1-ol) to propenal (acrolein).

questions.solution:
(i)(I) When 1 mol of ethanal (CH3CHO) is treated with 1 mol of CH3OH in presence of dry HCl, a hemiacetal is formed: CH3CHO + CH3OH → CH3CH(OH)(OCH3) (1-methoxyethanol / hemiacetal). With excess alcohol it would give the full acetal.

(II) Benzaldehyde has no alpha-hydrogen, so it undergoes Cannizzaro reaction with conc. NaOH. One molecule is oxidised and another is reduced: 2C6H5CHO + NaOH(conc.) → C6H5COONa (sodium benzoate) + C6H5CH2OH (benzyl alcohol).

(III) When ethanoic acid (CH3COOH) is heated in presence of P2O5 (a dehydrating agent), acetic anhydride is formed: 2CH3COOH → (CH3CO)2O + H2O. P2O5 removes water to promote anhydride formation.

(ii) To distinguish between ethanal (CH3CHO) and propanal (CH3CH2CHO): Iodoform test — add I2 solution and NaOH (or Na2CO3). Ethanal gives a yellow precipitate of iodoform (CHI3) because it has the CH3CO- group. Propanal does not give a yellow precipitate as it lacks the methyl ketone grouping.

(iii) To convert allyl alcohol (CH2=CH-CH2OH, prop-2-en-1-ol) to propenal (CH2=CH-CHO, acrolein), the reagent used is MnO2 (manganese dioxide) or PCC (Pyridinium Chlorochromate). These mild oxidising agents selectively oxidise the allylic alcohol to the corresponding aldehyde without affecting the double bond.

questions.text_english:
(b) (i) Draw the structure of the semicarbazone of acetone.
(ii) Why are α-hydrogen atoms of aldehydes and ketones acidic in nature?
(iii) Arrange the following compounds in increasing order of their reactivity towards HCN:
CH3COCH3, CH3CHO, (CH3)3C-CO-CH3
(iv) Write the reaction involved in Etard reaction.
(v) Write the product when cyclohexane-CHO reacts with Zn(Hg)/conc. HCl.

key_points: (i) Structure of acetone semicarbazone: CH3-C(=N-NH-CO-NH2)-CH3
(ii) Alpha-H is acidic because the carbonyl group (C=O) withdraws electrons, stabilising the carbanion/enolate formed by loss of alpha-H.
(iii) Increasing reactivity towards HCN: (CH3)3CCOCH3 < CH3COCH3 < CH3CHO (steric and electronic effects)
(iv) Etard reaction: toluene + CrO2Cl2 (chromyl chloride) → chromium complex → hydrolysis → benzaldehyde
(v) Cyclohexane-CHO + Zn(Hg)/conc.HCl (Clemmensen reduction) → cyclohexane-CH3 (methylcyclohexane)

questions.solution:
(i) The semicarbazone of acetone is formed by the reaction of acetone with semicarbazide (NH2-NH-CO-NH2). Structure: CH3-C(=N-NH-CO-NH2)-CH3 (the C=O of acetone is replaced by C=N-NHCONH2).

(ii) Alpha-hydrogen atoms in aldehydes and ketones are acidic because the carbonyl group (C=O) adjacent to the alpha-carbon withdraws electron density through induction and resonance. When the alpha-H is removed, the resulting carbanion (enolate ion) is stabilised by resonance — the negative charge is delocalised onto the electronegative oxygen of the carbonyl group. This stabilisation lowers the energy of the carbanion, making the alpha-H relatively easy to remove (acidic).

(iii) Reactivity towards HCN (nucleophilic addition) depends on: (a) electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon (more positive character = more reactive); (b) steric accessibility. Electron-donating groups (alkyl groups) decrease electrophilicity; bulky groups create steric hindrance. CH3CHO has one methyl group (less hindered, more electrophilic), CH3COCH3 has two methyl groups, and (CH3)3C-CO-CH3 has a very bulky tert-butyl group and is most hindered. Increasing order of reactivity towards HCN: (CH3)3C-CO-CH3 < CH3COCH3 < CH3CHO.

(iv) Etard reaction: Toluene (or an alkyl benzene) reacts with chromyl chloride (CrO2Cl2) in CS2 to form a reddish-brown chromium complex (Etard complex), which on hydrolysis with water gives benzaldehyde (or the corresponding aryl aldehyde): C6H5-CH3 + 2CrO2Cl2 → C6H5-CH(CrOCl2)2 (Etard complex) → H2O → C6H5-CHO (benzaldehyde) + Cr products.

(v) When cyclohexanecarbaldehyde (cyclohexane-CHO) reacts with Zn(Hg)/conc. HCl (Clemmensen reduction), the aldehyde group (-CHO) is reduced to a methyl group (-CH3). Product: methylcyclohexane (cyclohexane-CH3).
